sections.ingredients:

 Haritaki (Terminalia chebula) – Chebulic Myrobalan 
 Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica) – Belleric Myrobalan 
 Amalaki (Emblica officinalis) – Indian Gooseberry 


 Quantity 

 Triphala – 2½ seer (approximately 2.3–2.5 kg) 
 Water – 20 seer (approximately 18–19 liters) 

 The prepared distillate is collected in approximately 20 bottles according to the classical method. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 Equal parts of Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bibhitaki (Terminalia bellirica), and Amalaki (Emblica officinalis) are taken and coarsely powdered (Jaukut Churna). 
 Around 2 1⁄2 seer (approximately 2.4 kg) of the coarse Triphala mixture is soaked overnight in 20 seer (approximately 18–19 liters) of water. 
 On the following morning, the soaked material is transferred into a traditional distillation apparatus known as Bhabka Yantra. 
 The mixture is heated gently, and the vapors are condensed carefully to obtain the distilled extract known as Triphala Ark. 
 The collected Ark is filtered and stored in clean glass bottles for medicinal use. 

 The preparation should always be stored in airtight containers away from direct sunlight to maintain potency.

 Triphala Ark is traditionally used in Prameha and Madhumeha (Diabetes Mellitus) because it helps regulate metabolism and supports proper tissue nourishment. It may assist in reducing excessive urination, sluggish metabolism, and accumulation of unhealthy fat tissues.

 2. Blood Purification and Skin Health 
 This Ark is considered an excellent Rakta Shodhak (blood purifier). It is beneficial in: 

 Acne 
 Itching 
 Eczema 
 Chronic skin disorders 
 Fungal infections 
 Pama (scabies-like conditions) 
 Kushtha (chronic skin diseases) 

 By improving digestion and eliminating toxins from the bloodstream, it helps improve skin complexion and natural glow. 

 3. Supports Digestion and Relieves Constipation 
 Triphala Ark improves digestive fire (Agni) without causing excessive heat. It is useful in: 

 Indigestion 
 Loss of appetite 
 Flatulence 
 Abdominal heaviness 
 Constipation 

 Its mild bowel-cleansing action helps remove accumulated waste material while supporting healthy intestinal function. 

 4. Useful in Obesity and Excess Sweating 
 The formulation is traditionally recommended in: 

 Medovriddhi (obesity) 
 Excessive perspiration 
 Foul body odor 

 By correcting metabolism and removing toxins, it helps maintain internal cleanliness and healthier body function. 

 5. Beneficial in Liver Disorders and Jaundice 
 Triphala Ark supports liver function and is traditionally used in: 

 Pandu (anemia-like disorders) 
 Kamala (jaundice) 
 Sluggish liver function 

 The detoxifying nature of Triphala helps improve bile regulation and supports healthier digestion and nutrient assimilation. 

 6. Useful in Chronic Inflammatory Conditions 
 Ayurveda describes Triphala Ark as beneficial in: 

 Amavata (rheumatic disorders) 
 Vatarakta (gout-like conditions) 
 Chronic inflammatory disorders 

 Its detoxifying and anti-inflammatory actions help reduce toxin accumulation responsible for joint discomfort and stiffness. 

 Modern studies on Triphala indicate the presence of important phytochemicals such as: 

 Tannins 
 Gallic acid 
 Ellagic acid 
 Vitamin C 
 Flavonoids 
 Polyphenols 

 These compounds demonstrate antioxidant, digestive-supportive, antimicrobial, and detoxifying properties. Triphala is widely studied for its role in supporting gut health, metabolism, immunity, and skin wellness. Because Ark preparations are lighter and rapidly absorbable, Triphala Ark may provide quicker systemic action compared to heavier formulations.

 Introduction

 The collected Ark is filtered and stored in clean glass bottles for medicinal use. 
 
 The preparation should always be stored in airtight containers away from direct sunlight to maintain potency. 

 Dosage and Administration 
 
 Dose: 2 to 8 tola (approximately 24–96 ml) 
 Frequency: 3–4 times daily according to the condition 
 It may be administered alone or mixed with an equal quantity of water. 
 
 The dosage should be adjusted according to age, digestive capacity, and disease severity under Ayurvedic supervision
